note: Missing hamza in أكون; smooth learner-facing phrasing.
Current ما نحتاج is incomplete/awkward in standard learner-facing Arabic; use ما نحتاج إليه.
عرفنا is past ('we learned/knew'); English is present 'we know'.
بماذا تفكر is awkward after أخبرني; standard phrasing is بما تفكر فيه.
Standard spelling is اهتمام, not إهتمام.
With people, standard relative construction is من لدي rather than ما لدي.
Arabic includes الآن ('now'), omitted by English.
proposed_english: You can open your eyes now.

note: Current Arabic means 'Your words remind me of my wife', not 'You sound like my wife'.
proposed_english: What you say reminds me of my wife.

note: بمقدورنا الأكل هنا only asks whether eating here is possible; 'afford' requires cost/financial ability.
proposed_target: هل يمكننا تحمّل تكلفة الأكل هنا؟
proposed_english: Can we afford to eat here?

note: السلطعون means crab; 'carp' is سمك الشبوط. Also أن needs hamza.
proposed_target: هل تعلم أن سمك الشبوط يأكل الشراغف؟
proposed_english: Did you know carp eat tadpoles?

note: رخصتك is generic 'your license'; English specifically says driver's license.
proposed_english: Do you have your driver's license?

note: فهمت is 'did you understand', not 'do you know'.
proposed_english: Did you understand what I mean?
